subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw permanently own a custom cooperative extra-bootstrap glob walker and yield between `agent:bootstrap` hook handlers as the runtime contract for responsiveness?
rationale: The branch deliberately changes two shared runtime contracts—filesystem matching and hook scheduling—where green targeted tests and a benchmark cannot determine the preferred long-term compatibility boundary.

options.title: Approve the cooperative contract
options.body: Accept the custom walker and bootstrap-only hook yields, with the tested Node-glob parity envelope treated as a maintained runtime contract.

options.title: Narrow the patch
options.body: Keep only an owner-approved responsiveness mitigation that avoids taking ownership of broad custom glob-parity and hook-scheduling semantics.

options.title: Pause for a design owner
options.body: Leave the PR open until the agent-runtime owner defines the intended filesystem and hook-interleaving guarantees.

recommendation.title: Approve the cooperative contract
recommendation.body: Accept the custom walker and bootstrap-only hook yields, with the tested Node-glob parity envelope treated as a maintained runtime contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Explicitly routed in the PR timeline and the decision concerns shared runtime behavior rather than the contributor's branch mechanics.
